newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures still up late but in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures still up late but in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained modestly higher Friday in lackluster late trade, helped by prospects for colder weather next week but prices were still stuck in recent technical ranges, sources said.
At 1425 EST, December climbed 4.7 cents to $2.69 per million British thermal units. January was 4.6 cents higher at $2.695. Others were up by one to 4.2 cents.

"Cash is holding, and we found some paper support early," said one New York-based futures trader, adding forecasts for colder weather have helped buoy the complex but only sustained cold could drive prices much higher.

Temperatures in the Northeast are expected to fall to 15 degrees below-normal by Monday and Tuesday. In most of the Midwest temperatures also are forecast to be significantly below-normal through the early part of next week. But much of the rest of the country will be normal to above-normal.
Technically, traders said recent ranges were intact, with good support in December in the $2.52-2.53 area and resistance at $2.745 and then at the $2.88 contract high.

Cash sources said weekend Gulf Coast prices were unchanged Friday at about $2.70. Midwest pipes also held relatively steady in the high-$2.50s. Forecasts for colder weekend weather drove New York city gate gas prices up a dime or more to the $3.05-3.15 range.
NYMEX said 16,146 Hub contracts traded at 1400 EST. NYMEX Henry Hub open interest on Nov 7 gained 2,179 contracts to 147,170.
NYMEX Alberta natgas was still untraded at 1420 EST, but December was bid two cents higher at $1.29.
NYMEX Permian natgas also was untraded at 1420 EST, with December offered a penny higher at $2.50.
On the KCBT, December eased one-half cent to $2.485, while January was one cent higher at $2.48. The December East/West spread widened by 5.2 cents to 20.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
